run.mjs.role: Bounded pg_ctl startup/shutdown subprocess wait repair and startup-phase failure recording

triggerEvidence.interpretation: The database became ready but no preflight or scenario evidence was produced. The 35-second runner deadline plus 5-second termination wait, with successful owned cleanup, supports an inherited-pipe close wait during pg_ctl start; this is a diagnosis, not proof of database behavior.

changes: Captured commands retain stdout/stderr capture and close-event completion semantics.
pg_ctl start and stop use ignored stdio and wait for the spawned command exit code, avoiding inherited daemon pipe handles while retaining bounded deadlines.

pg_ctl timeout terminates only its direct child, never recursively taskkills a possibly started PostgreSQL process; ambiguous cleanup remains UNKNOWN behind the existing private ownership marker and PID/path/port/loopback checks.

Startup rejects an unexpected preexisting postmaster.pid, verifies the newly created PID-file data path/port/loopback identity, and confirms the loopback listener within a bounded retry window before writing connection credentials.
The final evidence manifest now records failedPhase plus bounded failure code/message without stack or environment data.
limitations: No PostgreSQL runner/database execution was performed after this repair; root must review and execute under the original authorization contract.
This addresses the observed launcher wait/diagnostic gap only and does not assert scenario or database behavior PASS.
